question.text: How many Falcon 9 or Falcon Heavy orbital launches will SpaceX have in the second half of November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the number of launches of Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy launch vehicles occurring between November 16, 2026 and November 30, 2026 (inclusive of both dates and in UTC), according to Wikipedia's [List of Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy launches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Falcon_9_and_Falcon_Heavy_launches#2026).
question.fine_print: Admins will use their discretion if there appears to be an [edit war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Edit_warring) or lack of Wikipedia [consensus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Consensus) and may rely on [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/help/faq/#definitions) for additional verification.

# SpaceX Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy launches, Nov 16 to 30, 2026: research summary

Bottom line: no Falcon launches have happened in the Nov 16-30 window yet. Falcon flights have slowed a lot in recent weeks. My rough count of reasonably firm candidates for the window is about 3 to 5, with up to 3 undated November missions that could add to that.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-12: The Wikipedia list says "as of November 12, 2026," SpaceX has flown 123 Falcon-family launches in 2026 (120 Falcon 9, 3 Falcon Heavy). The latest entry is F9-702. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Falcon_9_and_Falcon_Heavy_launches)
- Recent rows in the table (raw wikitext): Sep 6, 10, 13, 17, 20, 26; Oct 1 (Crew-13), Oct 1 (Transporter-18), Oct 2 (Falcon Heavy NROL-97), Oct 10, 13, 13, 16, 20, 23, 27, 31; Nov 7 (USSF-432); Nov 12 (USSF-627). [Wikipedia raw](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Falcon_9_and_Falcon_Heavy_launches&action=raw)
- Wikipedia's "future" list for November 2026:
  - Nov 15: USSF-317
  - Nov 18: USSF-266
  - Nov 29: Cygnus NG-25
  - "Nov," no date: OneWeb #21, Starlink Group 15-21, NROL-195

## 2. Current status
- Nothing is settled. No launches have happened in the window yet, and November has only 2 Falcon launches so far.
- A Nov 10 SDA launch reported by TechTimes does not appear in Wikipedia. Spaceflight Now and Wikipedia date the SDA Tranche 1 Transport Layer A launch to Oct 10. The Wikipedia count also fits USSF-627 being the 120th Falcon 9 flight. The TechTimes date is probably wrong.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-13: USSF-317 has slipped several times: first Nov 12, then Nov 13, now Sat Nov 14 at 7:55 pm PT (03:55 UTC Nov 15). It counts only if it slips again to Nov 16 UTC or later. [Rocketlaunch.org](https://rocketlaunch.org/launch-schedule/spacex), [Next2Space](https://next2space.com/), [aktualita](https://aktualita.co/en/technology-ai/spacex-ussf-317-launch-delay-falcon-9-time-watch-live)
- 2026-11-13: SpaceNexus lists 10 SpaceX launches for November:
  - Nov 18 03:14 UTC: USSF-266
  - Nov 18 16:49 UTC: USSF-317 (Wikipedia and other trackers say Nov 15 for this one)
  - Nov 21: NROL-136 (this listing appears only on SpaceNexus)
  - Nov 29: NG-25
  - No date: Starlink 15-21, OneWeb 21, NROL-195
  - Starship Flight 15 on Nov 13. Starship launches do not count for this question. [SpaceNexus](https://spacenexus.us/launches/spacex/2026-11)
- 2026-11-12: USSF-627 launched from Vandenberg (04:36 UTC), the second classified Space Force launch in six days. [Space.com](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/spacex-launches-2nd-mystery-mission-for-us-space-force-in-6-day-span-photos)
- NG-25: Northrop Grumman says Falcon 9 from SLC-40, NET late November. Trackers give Nov 29 or Nov 30, and one gives Dec 31 as a placeholder. [Northrop Grumman](https://www.northropgrumman.com/what-we-do/space/missions/nasa-commercial-resupply-mission-ng-25), [Orbitalradar](https://orbitalradar.com/launch/falcon-9-cygnus-crs-2-ng-25)
- 2026-11-01: AS USA, via Jumpseat, reported "at least seven" SpaceX launches scheduled for November, including Starship. [Jumpseat](https://jumpseataerospacenews.com/2026/11/spacex-launch-schedule-for-november-2026/)
- Fewer Starlink flights: Space.com reports that Starlink 10-49 in August was the last Falcon 9 Starlink launch from Florida. Gaps between West Coast Starlink launches have also widened. [Space.com](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/spacex-falcon-9-starlink-group-15-15-b1063-ocisly), [newspaceeconomy](https://newspaceeconomy.ca/2026/10/28/how-will-spacex-manage-the-falcon-9-to-starship-transition-through-2029/)
- Gwynne Shotwell, SpaceX's president, guided to "maybe 140, 145-ish" Falcon 9 launches in 2026. That leaves about 20-25 more in roughly 7 weeks. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Falcon_9_and_Falcon_Heavy_launches)

## 4. Base rates
Half-month Falcon counts, taken from the Wikipedia table (Sep 2 from Spaceflight Now):

| Period | Launches |
|---|---|
| Sep 1-15 | 4 |
| Sep 16-30 | 3 |
| Oct 1-15 | 6 (incl. Falcon Heavy) |
| Oct 16-31 | 5 |
| Nov 1-15 | 2, or 3 if USSF-317 flies by Nov 15 |

- Earlier in 2026 the pace was much higher: 94 Falcon 9 flights by Aug 11, about one every 2.4 days. That works out to roughly 6 per half-month. [Newzino](https://newzino.com/story/spacex-launch-cadence-2026)
- Since Aug 11 there have been 26 Falcon 9 flights in about 3 months, roughly 4.3 per half-month.
- Half-month counts since September have ranged from 2 to 6.

## 5. Other forecasts
These markets cover all of November, not just Nov 16-30.
- Kalshi, "SpaceX launches in November": Above 6 at 97%, above 7 at 85%, above 8 at 56%, above 9 at 6%. This probably counts all SpaceX launches, including Starship; check the rules.
  - If the first half ends up at 2 Falcon flights, plus USSF-317 on Nov 15 and Starship Flight 15, that is about 4 launches. A November total of about 8-9 would then imply about 4-5 Falcon launches in Nov 16-30.
- Polymarket, "SpaceX launches in November 2026": under 13 at 90%, 13 at 8%, 14+ at about 10% combined.
- Kalshi, Starship Flight 15: 66% before Nov 14, 77% before Nov 15. This does not affect the Falcon count directly, but it matters for reading the Kalshi monthly market above.
- I found no market or Metaculus forecast for this exact Nov 16-30 Falcon question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- USSF-317 (Vandenberg): targeting 03:55 UTC Nov 15. A slip of one day or more moves it into the window.
- USSF-266 (Vandenberg): Nov 18.
- NROL-136: Nov 21. Only SpaceNexus lists it, so it is unconfirmed.
- NG-25 (Cape Canaveral): Nov 29-30. It could slip into December.
- Undated November missions: Starlink 15-21, OneWeb #21, NROL-195. Any of them could fall in the window or slip.
- Q4 missions with no firm dates: SDA Tranche 1 Transport Layer D and F, Tracking Layer C, BlueBird 14-16, CHORUS, Globalstar.
- Risks: any Falcon 9 anomaly or grounding, weather, and Vandenberg range conflicts. Most of the candidate launches fly from Vandenberg.

Sources: [Wikipedia list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Falcon_9_and_Falcon_Heavy_launches), [SpaceNexus](https://spacenexus.us/launches/spacex/2026-11), [Next Spaceflight](https://nextspaceflight.com/launches/?f=agency_1), [Spaceflight Now log](https://spaceflightnow.com/launch-log/), [Space.com](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/spacex-launches-2nd-mystery-mission-for-us-space-force-in-6-day-span-photos), [Newzino](https://newzino.com/story/spacex-launch-cadence-2026), [Jumpseat](https://jumpseataerospacenews.com/2026/11/spacex-launch-schedule-for-november-2026/), [Northrop Grumman](https://www.northropgrumman.com/what-we-do/space/missions/nasa-commercial-resupply-mission-ng-25), [Rocketlaunch.org](https://rocketlaunch.org/launch-schedule/spacex), [Explore Lompoc](https://explorelompoc.com/event/rocket-launch-space-x-ussf-317/), [TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/330547/20261112/spacex-falcon-9-launches-another-classified-space-force-mission-just-six-days-after-ussf-432.htm)

Only the headline figures and the January 2026 entries came through, so I could not count launches per month directly from the source. ## 4. Base rates

- 2025: 165 Falcon 9 launches, about 6.8 per 15 days. [Space.com](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/spacex-falcon-9-starlink-group-15-15-b1063-ocisly)
- 2026 year to date: 123 Falcon launches in about 316 days, about 5.8 per 15 days. The pace was higher earlier in the year and has dropped since late summer.
- If the 140-145 guidance holds, about 17-22 more launches would be needed in the last 49 days of the year, about 5-7 per 15 days. That looks optimistic given recent cadence.
- Recent pace: 3 launches from November 1-12. October had roughly 10-11 SpaceX launches, based on Kalshi's resolved-looking market (Above 10 at 0.99, Above 11 at 0.02). Known October missions include a Falcon Heavy on October 1, SDA on October 9, Starlink on October 12, CRS on October 13, USSF on October 15, Starlink on October 20, Starlink on October 27, and Starlink on October 30/31 (the 700th Falcon 9). That works out to about 5 per 15 days lately. [Spaceflight Now search results](https://spaceflightnow.com/2026/10/), [AIAA](https://aiaa.org/?p=37589)

## 5. Other forecasts

- Kalshi, "SpaceX launches in November" (this probably includes Starship, so check the rules): Above 6 at 0.97, Above 7 at 0.85, Above 8 at 0.56, Above 9 at 0.06. The implied median is about 9 for the whole month.
  - Rough arithmetic: subtract 3 Falcon launches from November 1-12, about 1 Starship flight, and USSF-317 if it flies November 13-15. That implies roughly 4-5 Falcon launches in the window. This is my approximation, not the market's own figure.
- Polymarket, "SpaceX launches in November 2026": <13 at 0.90, 13 at 0.08, 14+ at about 0.10 combined.
- Kalshi, Starship Flight 15 before November 15: 0.77. A Starship flight would not count toward this question.
- I found no forecast that targets November 16-30 specifically.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution

- USSF-317, November 15 (or later). Whether it slips past 00:00 UTC on November 16 is the main swing factor.
- USSF-266, November 18; NROL-136, November 21; NG-25, November 29. NG-25 is close to the end of the window, so a slip of 2 days or more would push it out.
- Starlink 15-21, OneWeb 21 and NROL-195 could fill the gaps, but none has a date yet.
- Risks that could lower the count: weather, scrubs at Vandenberg, which is carrying almost the whole manifest, and any Falcon anomaly or stand-down.

Sources: the URLs linked above, plus [spacelaunchschedule](https://www.spacelaunchschedule.com/), [flightatlas](https://www.flightatlas.org/trackers/spacex), [rocketlaunch.org](https://rocketlaunch.org/launch-schedule/spacex) and [ChainCatcher](https://www.chaincatcher.com/en/article/2303467).

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** The window runs Nov 16 to 30 UTC, starting in about 3 days. The outcome is known around Dec 1, roughly 18 days from now.

(b) **Status quo:** The recent pace is 2 to 5 Falcon launches per half-month. Firm-ish candidates in the window are USSF-266 (Nov 18) and NG-25 (Nov 29, could slip to December). Possible additions are NROL-136 (Nov 21, unconfirmed), Starlink 15-21, OneWeb 21, NROL-195, and USSF-317 if it slips past Nov 15. The status quo lands at about 3 to 4.

(c) **Base rates:**
* Half-month counts since September were 4, 3, 6, 5, and 2 or 3. Three to four is the modal bucket, five to six is next, and two or fewer occurred once.
* Earlier in 2026 the pace was about 6 per half-month, but cadence has clearly fallen as Florida Starlink launches ended.
* Shotwell's guidance of 140 to 145 would imply about 6 per half-month. That looks stale given recent pace.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
* Nov 12: Wikipedia shows only 2 Falcon launches so far in November.
* Nov 13: USSF-317 is targeting 03:55 UTC Nov 15. It falls just outside the window unless it slips a day.
* Nov 13: Kalshi prices total SpaceX November launches, including Starship, at 9 or more at 56% and 8 or more at 85%. Assume about 4 launches by Nov 15: 2 Falcon, USSF-317, and probably Starship Flight 15. That implies about 4 to 5 Falcon launches in the second half, which leans toward the top of Three or Four and Five or Six.
* SpaceNexus lists 10 SpaceX launches in November, including several undated ones.
* NG-25 is "NET late November," so it is at real risk of slipping into December.

(e) **Unexpected scenario:**
* Low side: a Falcon 9 anomaly or grounding, plus slips of NG-25 and the undated missions, leaves only USSF-266, giving two or fewer.
* High side: USSF-317 slips into the window, and NROL-136, Starlink 15-21, OneWeb, NROL-195 and NG-25 all fly, giving seven or more.

**Adjustment:** I started from recent base rates, which center on 3 to 4. I moved somewhat toward 5 to 6 because of the Kalshi monthly market and the number of undated November missions. I kept 3 to 4 as the mode because the recent slowdown and schedule slips are real.
